articles.title: Psychology says a cluttered home may be linked to more than visual mess; a 2025 study of 501 adults associated household clutter with lower psychological well-being and life satisfaction
articles.summary: Household clutter was linked with lower psychological well-being in a 2025 study of 501 adults.
articles.body: Household clutter was linked with lower psychological well-being in a 2025 study of 501 adults. The survey by Francis Quinn collected data from May 2020 to November 2021. According to the study published in ScienceDirect, titled ‘Home clutter and mental well-being: Exploring moderators and the mediating role of home beauty’, people who rated their homes as more cluttered reported lower mental well-being, lower life satisfaction and less positive feeling, along with more negative feeling. The author reports that how beautiful people found their home explained part of this link. The study did not measure restlessness, and the author states that a survey like this cannot show that clutter causes lower well-being.How researchers studied clutter and psychological well-beingAccording to the study, the research was an online survey carried out between May 2020 and November 2021, during the COVID-19 pandemic. It was advertised on participant recruitment websites and in a university's weekly email to students and staff. Anyone over 16 who understood English could take part. Three people who gave no information apart from their country were removed before the analysis. The paper says participants were offered entry into a prize draw for one of three £40 Amazon.com gift vouchers.The 501 participants were 80% women, 19% men and 1% another gender identity, aged from 16 to 92, with an average age of 33. According to the author, 33% were full-time students, 42% were renters, and 31% were self-isolating because of COVID. Most lived in the UK (84%), with smaller numbers elsewhere in Europe (5%), Asia (3%) and North America (3%). The survey asked people to rate how cluttered their homes were, including by room: the living room, bedroom, kitchen and bathroom. It also asked about their positive and negative feelings, their mental well-being, and how satisfied they were with life overallClutter was linked to lower life satisfaction and well-beingAccording to the study, the link between clutter and well-being pointed the same way every time. People who rated their homes as more cluttered reported lower mental well-being, lower life satisfaction and less positive feeling, along with more negative feeling. The paper gives figures for one of its two clutter measures: −.27 with mental well-being, −.26 with life satisfaction, −.22 with positive feelings and .25 with negative feelings. The author describes all of these links as small, and they were statistically significant.The paper says the same pattern held in its path model, where the effects were small to modest and clutter explained only about 6% to 7% of the variance in each outcome. The discussion notes that earlier studies, including Rogers and Hart (2021) and Roster et al. (2016), found medium-sized effects. The author suggests that the difference may come from who was recruited. According to the paper, some earlier studies drew many people who were interested in clutter or struggling with it, while this one took a more general approach to recruitment.How home beauty influenced the link between clutter and well-beingAccording to the paper, this was the first time that how beautiful people find their home had been tested as a link between clutter and well-being. Participants rated one statement, "The interior of my home is beautiful". The study found that people with more clutter tended to rate their homes as less beautiful. It also found that people who rated their homes as more beautiful tended to report better well-being, for example, a link of .43 with life satisfaction and .40 with positive feelings.The author reports that home beauty explained part of the connection between clutter and well-being, but not all of it. The direct links from clutter to well-being stayed significant, only smaller. The paper also says that people's general ability to appreciate beauty made no clear difference to these results. The author calls the home beauty finding tentative, partly because it relied on a single survey question, and says future work needs a longer set of questions to confirm it.Why clutter's link to well-being may not prove cause and effectResearchers also checked whether the clutter link differed between groups of people, including by age, gender, income, student status, time spent at home and intention to declutter. There were 32 possible differences to test, and only one came out as significant: time at home at weekends and its effect on positive feelings. The author writes that this does not appear likely to be a genuine effect, given the number of tests run and its very small size.The author states that a survey like this cannot show that clutter causes lower well-being. The paper says the data cannot rule out the opposite explanation: that people with lower well-being may let clutter build up. It also notes that the data were collected during the pandemic and that everything was self-reported. According to the abstract, the findings "are exploratory and require replication using longitudinal and/or experimental designs". The author says the results are consistent with the possibility that the home environment could affect well-being, though caution is needed about cause and effect.You use AI every day. articles.title: Lucknow's 13-year-old Aarna Om Singh set a record by performing 57 yoga poses in just 1 minute; she has also won more than 100+ medals and holds two world records for cartwheeling
articles.summary: At an age when most children are still developing understanding and discovering their interests, Lucknow’s 13-year-old Aarna Om Singh has already made her
articles.body: At an age when most children are still developing understanding and discovering their interests, Lucknow’s 13-year-old Aarna Om Singh has already made her parents proud. She has made a mark in the world of yoga and gymnastics by setting some commendable records. She recently performed 57 different yoga poses in just one minute. With this, the young girl showed remarkable flexibility, balance and speed. But this is only one of several achievements in her growing sporting journey.The young yoga lover has won over 100 medals at district, state, national and international level. She also holds two world records for cartwheeling, which is an incredible feat.Meet Aarna who has set record for 57 yoga poses in a minuteAarna was born on February 11, 2013 studying in City Montessori School (CMS), Gomti Nagar Campus I. As per the Asia Book of Records entry published on September 12, 2026, Aarna performed 57 yoga poses in one minute, setting a record for the maximum number of yoga poses performed in a minute by a teenager.Performing 57 different yoga poses under such a record duration not only requires physical flexibility but also immense body control, transitioning quickly and coordinating movements. For a young practitioner, the achievement reflects years of discipline.How yoga became an important part of her childhoodAarna's association with yoga started much earlier. As per her accounts, she had been practising yoga since the age of four and found the discipline relaxing.However, her journey towards becoming a competitive yoga practitioner took shape only during the Covid-19 lockdown. Her grandfather, Bharat Kumar Singh, inspired her as he himself practised yoga.What began as an opportunity to learn yoga at home gradually developed into a serious interest. Regular practice helped her understand different asanas and their techniques, while her participation in competitions gave her opportunities to test her abilities.Besides yoga, Aarna also learned mixed martial arts, gymnastics, Kathak, Bharatanatyam and writing. Her exposure to different activities helped her develop an interest in movement and physical fitness.Two world records for cartwheelingShe was 11 years old in 2025 when she made two records recognised by the Yogasana Book of World Records Council. According to a March 2025 report based on information shared by City Montessori School, she completed 45 cartwheels in 60 seconds which is another incredible achievement. Later, she performed 135 cartwheels in three minutes and 56 seconds.Her achievements also brought recognition from her school. CMS felicitated her for the double record feat, with school officials acknowledging her dedication and sporting accomplishments.More than 100 medals and international recognitionAarna's achievements extend well beyond record-setting performances. According to EducationWorld, her medal tally had crossed 100 by January 2026, with awards across district, state, national and international competitions.One of her notable achievements came at the 2025 Asia Pacific Yogasana Sports Championship in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. Competing against participants from several countries, she won a gold medal in traditional yogasana and a silver medal in artistic yogasana. She was also awarded the Champion of Champions trophy for her overall performance.She had also won gold at the CISCE National Games 2024 in the Under-14 girls' individual rhythmic yoga category. In addition, she received a silver medal at Dubai Expo 2020 when she was nine years old.An author with two booksAlongside her sporting achievements, she has authored two children's books: A Young Yog Girl (2023) and Adventures of Yog Nandini (2024).Despite her growing list of achievements, Aarna has bigger ambitions. In her January 2026 interview with EducationWorld, she expressed her desire to represent India at the Commonwealth Games and the Olympics. But for now, her journey continues through regular practice, competitions and new challenges.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ testGet the latest Lifestyle News and more. articles.title: COP31-UN climate talks enter second day of overtime amid fossil fuel row
articles.summary: Negotiators at the United Nations climate conference are reviewing a last-minute proposal from Turkish officials in an effort to overcome disagreements
articles.body: Negotiators at the United Nations climate conference are reviewing a last-minute proposal from Turkish officials in an effort to overcome disagreements and secure a final agreement.The COP31 summit in Antalya, Turkey, entered its second day of overtime on Sunday as countries remained divided over how to address the main causes of global warming, according to the news agency AP.Turkish environment minister Murat Kurum, who is chairing the two-week conference, said early Sunday that he had prepared a draft agreement acceptable to all participating nations.However, the proposal had not been made public, and it was unclear whether delegates had received the text in time to review it and suggest changes.The major points of disagreement include reducing dependence on fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas, promoting carbon capture and storage technology, and deciding whether increasing electricity demand should be met through renewable sources or also involve natural gas and coal.Kurum urged delegates to reach an agreement, reminding them that millions of people outside the conference venue were already experiencing the consequences of climate change.The talks were originally scheduled to conclude on Friday, but negotiations continued through the weekend. Meanwhile, an earlier draft of the final agreement faced criticism for not mentioning fossil fuels.Experts have warned that sharp reductions in emissions from coal, oil and gas are necessary to prevent the worst effects of global warming, including heatwaves, floods and other extreme weather events.Around 100 civil society organisations also criticised the slow progress, warning in a letter to co-hosts Turkey and Australia that COP31 risked becoming one of the most disappointing UN climate summits.The UN had warned before the conference that the world was likely to exceed the Paris Agreement target of limiting global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels.Teresa Anderson, global lead on climate justice at ActionAid International, said uncertainty continued over the outcome of the negotiations.Climate talks continue beyond deadlineThe conference venue in Antalya appeared largely deserted on Saturday as workers packed up equipment from exhibition areas and country pavilions. Corridors that had earlier been crowded with thousands of participants were mostly empty.Rachel Cleetus of the Union of concerned scientists said the extended negotiations had shown little progress, with concerns also growing over shortages of food and water at the venue.During the summit, climate action tracker warned that efforts to slow global warming had made little progress over the past five years, even as climate-related disasters became more severe. Recent examples include heatwaves in Europe and floods in Nepal.Climate-vulnerable countries, particularly small island nations facing rising sea levels, have called on wealthier nations to increase contributions to UN funds. They want financial assistance to recover from climate-related disasters and prepare for rising temperatures.Tuvalu's environment minister Maina Talia said frustration and mistrust among civil society groups, indigenous communities and vulnerable nations were increasing. However, he said he remained hopeful about the final agreement.The United States, one of the world's biggest polluters and largest economies, did not directly participate in this year's negotiations. The next climate summit is scheduled to take place in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, in November 2027.Protests add to criticism of COP31The negotiations also faced protests on Friday when a demonstrator wearing a red noose around his neck and a vest reading "you are killing the future" interrupted the proceedings.The protester climbed onto a table and demanded action against fossil fuels, warning that developing countries could not afford further delays in tackling climate change. Security personnel later escorted him out of the venue.The demonstration interrupted Kurum's address, prompting him to appeal for calm before continuing his speech.Harjeet Singh, a strategic adviser to the fossil fuel treaty initiative, said the venue had become quieter, although key negotiators and civil society representatives remained present. He added that major disagreements continued to delay progress, with no clear indication of when the talks would conclude.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Watch: Masked ICE agents drag away two at US’ Seattle airport, spark chaos during boarding
articles.summary: Masked Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers detained two people on a crowded jet bridge at United States' Seattle-Tacoma International
articles.body: Masked Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers detained two people on a crowded jet bridge at United States' Seattle-Tacoma International Airport while passengers were boarding a Los Angeles-bound flight on Saturday. The incident triggered a confrontation that delayed the departure and prompted concerns from Alaska Airlines and airport authorities.Video footage of the incident showed officers dragging away at least one person as a woman screamed that her daughter was being taken and had a work permit. The confrontation unfolded in front of passengers carrying their luggage, several of whom witnessed officers struggling with a person on the ground.In a statement, ICE said the operation was conducted to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, an immigrant from Mexico who had “overstayed his visa in violation of our nation’s laws.”The agency said another passenger, Sofia Hernandez Mejia, “hurled hot coffee on the officers” during the confrontation. ICE said she was also determined to be in the US illegally after overstaying her visa and could face charges of assaulting a federal officer.The incident occurred during boarding for Alaska Airlines flight 1306, which was scheduled to depart at 8:10 am for Los Angeles. Online flight data showed that the departure was delayed.Alaska Airlines said ICE had not informed it in advance about the enforcement action.“We are concerned by this morning’s law enforcement action during the boarding of Alaska Flight 1306,” the airline said in a statement.“We recognise how distressing this incident has been for affected employees and guests.”The airline added that it remained committed to “treating every guest with dignity and respect”. It said it was working with the Port of Seattle to determine whether established protocols had been followed and had raised its concerns “directly with the appropriate authorities”.The Port of Seattle, which manages the airport, also described the incident as distressing.In a statement, the port said the episode had affected not only the family involved but also other passengers. It added that local authorities would “engage federal officials to understand more about what occurred”.“We are outraged about this morning’s incident involving ICE and two passengers as travelers boarded AS 1306 to Los Angeles. Immigration enforcement actions at SEA are conducted without the Port’s participation or knowledge. The Port has continually asked, and local federal immigration authorities have previously agreed to protocols at SEA, and we are in conversation with DHS on whether any of these protocols were breached. However, the Port remains committed to the safety of all of our travelers and staff and airline team. This incident was not only distressing for the affected family but the passengers around them, and Port officials continue to engage federal officials to understand more about what occurred”, the port said.Washington governor Bob Ferguson criticised the enforcement operation, describing ICE's tactics as “deeply un-American” and calling for the agency to be abolished.“The video is horrific and it is chilling,” Ferguson said at an afternoon news conference attended by labour leaders and local elected officials.“We need a system of immigration enforcement and border security that is effective, ethical and humane. And ICE is not it. It is beyond reform.”Ferguson also said he was examining how federal agents accessed the jet bridge. He believed they had violated a state law he signed in March restricting the use of facial coverings by law enforcement officers.ICE has increased enforcement operations at airports since the summer, with particular attention to people suspected of overstaying visas.You use AI every day.
